issues: The wordmark used a real company name, SUPERHUMAN, and was only 64px tall with thin glowing lines, a narrow strip across the frame
The backdrop was three blurred purple blobs and a pink horizon line; it never read as a dusk landscape and the frame felt dull and grey-violet
Apart from the drawing there was almost no motion: the rest and hold segments were dead frames
Nothing resolved after the crystallisation; the last frame was a single thin line of text with no complete end card
changes: Sand look (beige with terracotta), moving from a dark dusk to a bright desert daybreak: a low white sun with halo, four procedural dune layers with atmospheric perspective (backlit ridge lines and near-ground wind ripples), horizon haze, high cloud wisps and drifting sand

The wordmark becomes a fictional brand, "SOLSTICE": eight single-line skeleton glyphs redrawn from x=0 and spaced by optical width, 103px cap height spanning 65% of the frame, 5px ink strokes, tracking about 0.6x cap height

The core rule is kept: every letter shares one progress value, starting and finishing on the same frame with continuous growth; a terracotta "hot ink" tip now rides each stroke and cools to ink as it finishes
A very slow push plus lateral truck moves the four dune layers at 1.5% / 3% / 5% / 8% for parallax; the sun rises throughout and its halo brightens one step as the word completes
Resolution: a 44px italic serif tagline "Your day, in better light." sharpens in from blur, then a 30f hold; duration 105 to 120f
